Educating Carolinians since 1595 EXPLORE PROJECTS CONNECT WITH US Institutional Information in Cebu City, PH University of San Carlos University of San Carlos (USC) is a Catholic educational institution administered since 1935 by the Society of the Divine Word (SVD) missionaries. A university since 1948, USC offers comprehensive undergraduate and graduate education. Learn more about Education with a Mission and how we Witness to the Word. 296 Faculty members actively engaged in research (AY 2020-23) 514 Papers published in international refereed journals (AY 2018-22) 46 Research collaboration agreements signed (AY 2017-21) 19 Patents Filed USD 5.1M External research grants (PHP301M, AY 2020-24) 8 CHED Centers of Excellence (COE) 12 CHED Centers of Development (COD) 16 Level III FAAP-accredited programs as evaluated by PAASCU 10 Level II FAAP-accredited programs as evaluated by PAASCU 7 PTC-ACBET-accredited programs Administered by the Society of the Divine Word (Societas Verbi Divini, SVD) since 1935, the University of San Carlos (USC) traces its roots to the Colegio de San Ildefonso, founded in August 1595 in Cebu City. The school closed in 1769 following the expulsion of Jesuit priests from the Philippines, and was reopened in 1783 as Colegio–Seminario de San Carlos, which operated until the college split from the seminary in 1930. Following another brief closure during World War II, Colegio de San Carlos reopened in 1945 and became a University in 1948. Rapid growth in the ‘50s saturated the campus near the city center, prompting expansion of the University to what was then called the Boys’ High School in 1956 (now San Carlos School of Cebu North Campus), and to the Teacher Education Center and Girls’ High School (now San Carlos School of Cebu South Campus), as well as to Talamban Campus in 1964. The total land area of the University’s two campuses is almost 88 hectares (or 217 acres), with about 78 hectares in Talamban Campus alone, and potentially ample room for future growth. Today, the University is one of the most respected higher education institutions in the Philippines, offering 43 undergraduate and 48 graduate and post-graduate programs. Many of these programs have received Level II or Level III accreditation from the Federation of Accrediting Associations of the Philippines (FAAP), as evaluated by the Philippine Accrediting Association of Schools, Colleges, and Universities (PAASCU). Seven engineering programs are also accredited by the Philippine Technological Council-Accreditation and Certification Board for Engineering and Technology (PTC-ACBET). The Philippine Commission on Higher Education (CHED) also granted Autonomous Status to the University, and designated eight Centers of Excellence (COE) and 12 Centers of Development (COD) in USC. Nearly 14,000 students in basic to graduate education are enrolled in the University, with over 200 international students. On average, the teacher-to-student ratio at USC is around 1:20. USC was ranked in the QS World University Rankings for Asia 2025, and is currently ranked 94th in Southeastern Asia and 507th in Asia in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2026. Recognized as a research hub in the southern Philippines, USC has drawn in external grants amounting to PHP 301M (~USD 5.1M) between AY 2020–2024, including the two pandemic-affected years. Research efforts are supported by a print collection of over 200,000 titles and almost 10,000 non-print volumes housed in the University’s Library System, along with subscriptions to Scopus and ScienceDirect. USC also publishes four scholarly journals: The Philippine Scientist , The Philippine Quarterly of Culture and Society , Devotio: Journal of Business and Economic Studies , and Tugkad: Literary and Cultural Studies Journal . Additional support for researchers is available through offices or committees providing ethics review, intellectual property and innovation and technology support, and animal care and use. Nineteen patents have been filed by the University since 2012, and one start-up company, Green Enviro Management Systems (GEMS), Inc., has been established. Student support in the University includes an international students’ office, online enrollment, dormitories, numerous cafes and canteens, and a transport system within Talamban Campus. USC has more than 200 undergraduate and graduate scholars at any given time. Since 2014, USC has been designated as a Donee Institution by the Philippine Council of Non-Governmental Organization Certification (PCNC). The University of San Carlos was recently ranked in the 2027 QS World University Rankings:Asia and the 2025 Times Higher Education Impact Rankings.
